# Chatbot test log

Ask each question on the live site (after clicking **Enable chat**), paste the chatbot's answer, then check it against the site guide and results. If the answer makes a claim the guide doesn't support, revise the guide or the system prompt and test again.

**Demo device / browser:** _(e.g., Windows laptop, Chrome 13x. WebGPU supported? yes/no)_

---

## 1. Data: "Where did your data come from?"
**What a correct answer should say:** the data is synthetic and computer-generated by the project's training notebook, not recorded from real people. It was loosely modeled on the UCI HAR smartphone dataset design (2.56 s windows at 50 Hz), with no UCI data used. It covers 30 simulated people and 3,600 windows.

**Chatbot answer:**
>

**Supported by the guide?** ☐ Yes ☐ Partly (what was wrong/added: ______) ☐ No

---

## 2. Results: "How did your model compare with the baseline?"
**What a correct answer should say:** on 720 test windows from 6 held-out people, the neural network scored 89.4% accuracy and the always-guess-one-activity baseline scored 33.3%, a gap of about 56 points. Most mistakes were walking vs. stairs up.

**Chatbot answer:**
>

**Supported by the guide?** ☐ Yes ☐ Partly (what was wrong/added: ______) ☐ No

## 3. Outside the guide: "How well would this model work on a dataset you never tested?"
**What a correct answer should say:** the guide doesn't say, because the model was never tested on another dataset. The answer should note that the data is simulated, so 89.4% should not be expected on real phone data. It should **not** give a made-up accuracy number.
